title: Expose cache_hit attribution + billed token fields in Usage API
author: Cole Summers
release_notes: Usage API now returns billed token fields (billed_prompt_tokens, billed_completion_tokens, billed_total_tokens) alongside raw tokens, and adds cache-hit attribution fields for supported endpoints. Backwards compatible: existing fields unchanged; new fields are additive and may be null for older events/backfilled periods.
body:
## Summary
This PR extends both the internal usage export and the customer-facing Usage API to include (1) billed tokens vs raw tokens, and (2) cache-hit attribution fields.

Why: Finance/RevRec and customers need to reconcile invoices against usage exports. Today the Usage API only returns token counts derived from request logs ("raw"), which can differ from what we bill after applying cache policies, retries/fallback dedupe, and endpoint normalization (OpenAI-compat vs native). Additionally, we’ve had multiple escalations where customers cannot explain a lower (or higher) invoice line item because they can’t see how much traffic was served from cache.

Scope:
- Adds new optional fields to usage rows returned by:
  - `GET /v1/usage` (customer)
  - `GET /internal/usage/export` (internal)
- Updates schema docs + SDK-facing JSON examples
- Adds guardrails around nullability + versioning to avoid breaking existing exports

Non-goals:
- Changing billing logic or meter definitions (handled in separate PRs / shadow billing compare)
- Backfilling historical rows (tracked in ENG-4412; this PR only ensures the fields can be carried end-to-end)

## API changes
### New fields (additive)
Token fields:
- `raw_prompt_tokens` (existing in some exports; now normalized)
- `raw_completion_tokens` (existing in some exports; now normalized)
- `raw_total_tokens` (derived)
- `billed_prompt_tokens` (NEW)
- `billed_completion_tokens` (NEW)
- `billed_total_tokens` (NEW)

Cache attribution fields:
- `cache_hit` (NEW, boolean-ish; may be null for legacy events)
- `cache_hit_type` (NEW; enum: `prefix_kv`, `full_response`, `none`, `unknown`)
- `cache_key_hash` (NEW; truncated, non-reversible; only returned on internal export)
- `cache_hit_tokens_saved` (NEW; optional; only populated when we can attribute savings)

Notes:
- Customer-facing endpoint does NOT return `cache_key_hash`.
- `cache_hit` may be null for older data or for endpoints that don’t support caching.
- `billed_*` fields reflect the meter output used by billing ledger aggregation (post-dedupe/idempotency and post-cache policy).

### Example response row
```
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-12T08:41:19Z",
  "account_id": "acct_9f3…",
  "project_id": "proj_2aa…",
  "endpoint": "chat.completions",
  "model": "rw-open-llama-3.1-70b",
  "region": "us-east-1",

  "raw_prompt_tokens": 812,
  "raw_completion_tokens": 226,
  "raw_total_tokens": 1038,

  "billed_prompt_tokens": 812,
  "billed_completion_tokens": 226,
  "billed_total_tokens": 1038,

  "cache_hit": false,
  "cache_hit_type": "none",
  "cache_hit_tokens_saved": 0
}
```

### Compatibility
- Existing clients reading token fields continue to work.
- New billed/cache fields are additive.
- We preserve existing naming where possible, but normalize internal export columns to avoid having two parallel token vocabularies.

## Implementation details
- Usage events already carry meter outputs in `usage_event.metered_*` (internal). This PR wires those through the aggregation layer and surface them in the API serializers.
- Adds `cache_hit_*` columns to the usage aggregation view; populated from request serving metadata when available.
- Introduces an internal `UsageRowVersion` (v1/v2) to make nullability/rollout explicit; customer endpoint always returns superset, with fields possibly null.
- Adds redaction: `cache_key_hash` is truncated and only included in internal export.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - serializer includes new fields when present
  - serializer keeps stable ordering/typing when fields are absent
- Integration tests:
  - end-to-end: usage event -> aggregation view -> API response
  - verifies customer endpoint never returns `cache_key_hash`
- Added golden JSON fixtures for:
  - cache miss
  - cache hit (prefix_kv)
  - legacy event (null cache fields)

## Ops / rollout
- Safe to merge behind default-on additive fields.
- Post-merge steps:
  1) Deploy to staging
  2) Have Finance validate on recon export (ENG-4438 table) for a sample account/day
  3) Enable for production (no feature flag required, but will be announced in internal changelog)

## Links
- Linear: ENG-4412 (backfill missing cache-hit fields), ENG-4438 (Snowflake export for Finance recon), PM-1842 (sanity-check KPIs)
- Support: SUP-28451 (invoice tokens do not match usage API), SUP-28522 (usage export timezone misalignment; not directly addressed here)

## Reviewer notes / risks
- Main risk is confusion between raw vs billed tokens. To mitigate, field names explicitly include `raw_` vs `billed_`, and docs call out that invoices use billed tokens.
- Nulls for cache attribution are expected for legacy rows; dashboards/recon queries must treat null as "unknown" not "false".

---
### Checklist
- [x] Backwards compatible
- [x] Internal export redaction for cache key material
- [x] Added tests + fixtures
- [x] Docs updated (internal API docstrings + examples)

docs: clarify raw vs billed token semantics in usage endpoint

conversation:
Nadia Rahman: Can we guarantee that billed_total_tokens == billed_prompt_tokens + billed_completion_tokens for all endpoints? Concern: tool-call/structured output attribution can cause confusing splits.
Cole Summers: Good call. For now the invariant holds for chat/completions + text generations. I added a comment + test asserting the invariant for supported endpoints and left others as "may be null" until the tool-call attribution work lands (see PR-27471).

Mei Lin: Please confirm Finance recon export will include both raw and billed tokens; we need billed for ledger match, raw for debugging anomalies.
Cole Summers: Confirmed. Internal export includes both sets. Customer endpoint includes both sets as well, but no cache_key_hash.

Monica Patel: Any SDK impact? We should avoid breaking existing parsing.
Cole Summers: Additive only. Field ordering not guaranteed; types stable. I added golden responses and ensured absent fields are omitted rather than zeroed to avoid misinterpretation.

Logan Wright: cache_hit null vs false matters. Can we document that null == unknown/unsupported? Also please avoid returning cache_hit_type when cache_hit is null.
Cole Summers: Updated docs + serializer: cache_hit_type omitted when cache_hit is null. Added test coverage.

Nikhil Sharma: For pricing experiments we need to segment on cache-hit to avoid confusing customers when billed tokens drop. Can we also surface cache_hit_tokens_saved?
Cole Summers: Added as optional field when available; currently populated for prefix_kv path only. Left null otherwise.
